## Monthly Budget Snapshot for $4,800 Take-Home Pay

These three plans all fit within income, but they optimize for different priorities: savings, debt paydown, and day-to-day flexibility.

## Budget Comparison and Best Fit

| Option | Total Allocated | Monthly Leftover | Savings Rate | Debt Repayment | Discretionary | Sustainability Read |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Option A | $4,800 | $0 | 14.6% | $500 | $1,250 | Balanced but tight on flexibility |
| Option B | $4,800 | $0 | 20.8% | $800 | $900 | Strongest overall balance and most aggressive on goals |
| Option C | $4,800 | $0 | 18.8% | $700 | $700 | Most conservative spending, but least flexible |

### What each option does best
- **Most sustainable:** **Option B**
  - Best mix of savings, debt repayment, and still reasonable discretionary spending.
  - It is the most resilient if you want progress without feeling overly restricted.
- **Maximizes savings:** **Option B**
  - Saves **$1,000/month**, the highest of the three.
  - That is **$12,000/year** going into savings.
- **Best balance between flexibility and debt reduction:** **Option B**
  - Debt repayment is also the highest at **$800/month**.
  - Discretionary spending stays healthier than Option C, so it is easier to maintain.

### Trade-offs by option
- **Option A**
  - Pros: Highest discretionary spending, decent savings.
  - Trade-off: Lowest savings and debt repayment, so long-term progress is slower.
- **Option B**
  - Pros: Best all-around plan; strongest savings and debt reduction with acceptable flexibility.
  - Trade-off: Less discretionary room than Option A.
- **Option C**
  - Pros: Controlled spending and solid savings.
  - Trade-off: Lowest flexibility; may feel restrictive month to month.

## Recommendation

**Choose Option B** if your goal is the best overall financial health.
It gives the strongest savings rate, the highest debt repayment, and still leaves enough discretionary spending to be sustainable.

If your priority is lifestyle flexibility above all else, **Option A** is the easier plan to live with. If your priority is strict spending control, **Option C** is the tightest.

## Sources

- Budgeting framework and debt prioritization guidance: https://www.consumer.gov/articles/1002-budgeting
- Savings and emergency fund planning: https://www.nerdwallet.com/article/finance/emergency-fund-why-it-matters
